name: Tuʻi Tonga Empire
summary: A Tongan maritime chiefdom (often called an empire) that spread its influence across West Polynesia from about 950, peaking between 1200 and 1500. Its double-hulled canoes linked islands across thousands of kilometres.

location.value: Tonga, centred on Tongatapu with its capital at Muʻa, with influence over Samoa, Fiji, Wallis (ʻUvea) and other islands.

terrain.value: Low coral and volcanic islands spread over a large ocean area.
terrain.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

climate.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

resources.value: Yams, taro, coconuts, fish; prestige goods such as fine mats and red feathers.
resources.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

disasters.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

population.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

urbanisation.value: Muʻa had royal tombs (langi) and a canal-linked harbour.
urbanisation.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

disease.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

migration.value: Polynesian voyaging spread people and goods between islands.
migration.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

economicBase.value: Farming and fishing, plus tribute brought to the Tuʻi Tonga.
economicBase.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

tradeRoutes.value: Modern researchers find evidence of transoceanic trade across West Polynesia.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.
wealth.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

moneyAndTax.value: No coinage; tribute in food, mats and tapa cloth (the ʻinasi ceremony).
moneyAndTax.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

inequality.value: Sacred chiefly lines at the top, commoners below.
inequality.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

governmentType.value: Monarchy under the sacred Tuʻi Tonga; later sharing power with the Tuʻi Haʻatakalaua and Tuʻi Kanokupolu.

keyRulers.value: ʻAhoʻeitu (first, c. 950), Tuʻitātui (built the Haʻamonga), Laufilitonga (last, 1827–1865).

succession.value: Hereditary in the sacred line; secular power passed to new royal lines.
succession.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

institutions.value: A division between sacred and secular rulers from the 15th century.
institutions.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

stability.value: Civil wars in Tonga in the early 19th century.
stability.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

eliteConflict.value: Rivalry between the three royal lines.
eliteConflict.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

armyAndTech.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

majorWars.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

territoryChange.value: Expanded its influence from about 950, peaking 1200–1500.

alliancesRivals.value: Close ties with Samoa and Fiji through marriage and war.
alliancesRivals.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

inventions.value: Large double-hulled voyaging canoes and star navigation.
inventions.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

scienceEducation.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

openness.value: Captain James Cook recorded the Tuʻi Tonga kings.

languageWriting.value: Tongan and other Polynesian languages; no writing.

artsArchitecture.value: The Haʻamonga ʻa Maui stone trilithon and royal stone tombs (langi).
artsArchitecture.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

socialStructure.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

sharedIdentity.value: The sacred status of the Tuʻi Tonga.
sharedIdentity.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

neighbours.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

ideasReligions.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

colonisation.value: Never colonised; Tonga stayed a monarchy.
colonisation.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

declineSignals.source: Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2017)

outcome.value: The title Tuʻi Tonga was abolished in 1865; modern Tonga is a constitutional monarchy.

sources.value: Oral traditions, archaeology and European accounts. Checked against Wikipedia (“Tuʻi Tonga Empire”).

overallCertainty.value: Low to medium. Some historians prefer “maritime chiefdom” to “empire”.

knownFor.label: Double-hulled voyaging canoes
knownFor.note: Large canoes that carried people and goods across open ocean.

knownFor.label: Polynesian wayfinding
knownFor.note: Navigation by stars, swells, winds and birds.
